positive:0.en: Master Qingwu set a small clay pot before me and folded her hands. 'Breathe the word slowly,' she said. The herb inside began to glow — a *positive* sign that my spirit root had accepted the formula. Shen Wujiu watched from the doorway, his eyes soft with quiet pride.
positive:0.cnHint: 师尊让我对着药草轻念咒字，药草发出光芒，这是____的信号，证明我的灵根已接受了法诀。
positive:0.hook: Then the glow flickered once — and went dark.
positive:0.line: 'That light is a *positive* sign — your root is alive.'

economic:0.en: The sect's inner hall held shelves of word-scrolls, each one priced by rarity. Master Qingwu traced the list with one finger. 'Every word has *economic* value here,' she said. 'A healing word feeds a village; a flight word buys a mountain.' I had arrived with nothing but breath.
economic:0.cnHint: 师尊在内堂向我解释每个咒字都有____价值，治愈之词能养活一整座村庄。
economic:0.hook: At the bottom of the list, one scroll had no price at all.
economic:0.line: 'A word's *economic* value rises when fewer disciples can speak it.'

link:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread a thin paper on the stone table and drew two circles. 'Each word is a *link* in a chain,' he said. 'Break one and the whole formula collapses.' Outside, wind moved through the hall like a slow breath, and the candle flame leaned toward the door.
link:0.cnHint: 师兄用图示向我说明每个咒字都是法诀链条中的一个____，断一环则全链崩溃。
link:0.hook: One circle on his drawing was already fading.
link:0.line: 'This word is the *link* between fire and wind — never drop it.'

produce:0.en: I pressed my palm to the jade plate and tried to *produce* a single tone of spiritual sound. Nothing came for a long moment. Then a thin hum rose, like silk tearing at the edge of hearing. Xiaoxing clapped once, softly, from her seat near the window.
produce:0.cnHint: 我试图用掌心在玉板上____一个灵音，沉默良久后，终于有细细的嗡鸣升起。
produce:0.hook: But the jade plate had cracked clean down the middle.
produce:0.line: 'You must *produce* a pure tone before the candle burns out.'

teach:0.en: 'I will *teach* you one word each morning,' Master Qingwu said, setting a single dried leaf on the desk between us. 'Speak it wrong and it heals nothing. Speak it right and it opens the next.' The room smelled of rain-wet stone and something older — like time pressed flat.
teach:0.cnHint: 师尊说每天清晨她会____我一个咒字，说错则无效，说对则开启下一个。
teach:0.hook: She had not yet told me how many mornings that would take.
teach:0.line: 'I can only *teach* you the door — you must walk through it yourself.'

worth:0.en: Xiaoxing handed me a scroll and whispered that it was *worth* three years of ordinary practice. 'Senior Shen traded a fire-word for it,' she added. I unrolled it slowly. The characters were so fine they looked like veins in a leaf, trembling in the lamplight.
worth:0.cnHint: 师妹告诉我这卷轴____三年的普通修炼，是师兄用一个火焰咒换来的。
worth:0.hook: A faint warmth moved through my fingers — then vanished.
worth:0.line: 'That scroll is *worth* more than anything else in this room.'

common:0.en: Master Qingwu told me that the word for 'still water' was the most *common* formula in the sect — every disciple learned it first. Yet she said it herself three times, and each time the air in the hall changed, as if the room were listening. I had not expected ordinary to feel so strange.
common:0.cnHint: 师尊说"静水"咒是门派里最____的法诀，人人先学，但她念出时整个厅堂的气息都随之变化。
common:0.hook: On the third breath, a thin crack appeared in the stone floor.
common:0.line: 'The most *common* word is also the one most disciples speak wrong.'

daily:0.en: Shen Wujiu showed me the practice board near the east window, worn smooth by years of hands. '*Daily* study of one word builds a root that even storm-wind cannot loosen,' he said, and tapped the wood twice. The board rang like a bell, low and long, out across the clouds below.
daily:0.cnHint: 师兄向我展示东窗旁被岁月磨光的练习板，说____修习一个咒字能筑牢任何风雨也动摇不了的根基。
daily:0.hook: The ringing did not fade — it grew.
daily:0.line: 'Your *daily* practice is the only thing that lasts here.'

policy:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a thin scroll above the altar stone. 'Every disciple must learn this,' she said. The sect's *policy* on forbidden words was clear: three were never to be spoken aloud, for each could crack the mountain roots. I copied the rule in silence, my brush shaking.
policy:0.cnHint: 师尊宣布了门派关于禁忌字词的____，弟子们必须严格遵守。
policy:0.hook: But the scroll listed only two forbidden words — not three.
policy:0.line: 'The *policy* of this sect protects every soul on this mountain.'

industry:0.en: Shen Wujiu ground ink for six hours without rest. 'The word for iron,' he said, 'demands *industry* — lazy hands cannot hold its power.' I watched his steady strokes fill the page and felt the air grow heavy and warm, as though the mountain itself approved. Then the lamp flame turned green.
industry:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，掌握'铁'字需要持续的____和勤奋，懒惰之人无法驾驭它的力量。
industry:0.hook: Green flame in the Cloud Sea Sect means something is listening.
industry:0.line: 'Without *industry*, no word will ever open for you.'

concern:0.en: Xiaoxing pressed her palm to my forehead and frowned. Her *concern* was not for my fever but for the silver mark the word 'wind' had left above my eye when I mispronounced it. 'It will fade,' she said softly, though her eyes told a different story. Outside, the clouds rose faster than usual.
concern:0.cnHint: 师妹对我额头上那道银色印记表示____，那是我念错'风'字后留下的痕迹。
concern:0.hook: Silver marks, the old texts say, are how the mountain counts its debts.
concern:0.line: 'My *concern* is that the mark is still bright after two hours.'

present:0.en: On the morning of my first full month, Master Qingwu placed a small jar on my desk. Inside rested a single dried petal — the word 'calm' pressed into its surface. 'This is your *present*,' she said. 'Use it only once.' I held the jar up to the window light, and the petal glowed faint gold.
present:0.cnHint: 师尊在我入门满月之日，送给我一份特别的____，那是一片刻有文字的花瓣。
present:0.hook: A gift from Master Qingwu always carries a second meaning.
present:0.line: 'Consider this *present* a promise — and a warning in equal measure.'

claim:0.en: A stranger in a grey robe stood at the sect gate and would not move. He began to *claim* that the word 'river' belonged to his school, not ours, and that we had stolen it three generations ago. Master Qingwu listened without blinking. When he finished, a single drop of rain fell from a clear sky.
claim:0.cnHint: 一名灰袍陌生人来到门派，____'河'字的所有权属于他们门派，并非我们所有。
claim:0.hook: One drop of rain from a clear sky is never an accident.
claim:0.line: 'I *claim* the word 'river' in the name of the Eastern Shore School.'

half:0.en: Shen Wujiu taught me that every healing word has two layers. I had mastered only the first. '*Half* a word,' he warned, 'can close a wound but leave the pain behind, like sealing a jar with the smoke still inside.' I practised the second layer all afternoon, and by dusk the candle flame leaned toward my page.
half:0.cnHint: 师兄警告我，只掌握了疗愈字词的____是危险的，会留下隐患。
half:0.hook: A candle that leans toward you is reading what you write.
half:0.line: '*Half* the word heals the body — the other half heals what the body forgets.'

successful:0.en: I released the word 'lift' for the first time and felt my feet leave the stone floor by three inches. Xiaoxing clapped once, quietly. 'You are *successful*,' she said, 'but keep your eyes open — height without sight is just falling in slow motion.' I landed softly, heart full, and noticed my shadow had not moved with me.
successful:0.cnHint: 我第一次成功施展'升'字，师妹说我____了，但也提醒我不能掉以轻心。
successful:0.hook: A shadow that stays behind is a shadow that knows something you do not.
successful:0.line: 'Being *successful* once means the word trusts you — do not break that trust.'

access:0.en: The inner library door had no handle and no lock. Master Qingwu said that only disciples who had memorised twenty root-words could *access* the texts within. I counted my own list that night: nineteen. I pressed my hand to the cold wood anyway, just to feel how close I was, and the door hummed once in the dark.
access:0.cnHint: 师尊说，只有背会二十个根字的弟子才能____内院藏书阁。
access:0.hook: Doors that hum have already decided whether to open.
access:0.line: 'You may *access* the inner shelves when the twentieth word lives in your bones.'

determine:0.en: Master Qingwu set three scrolls on the stone table before me. 'Read each one,' she said, 'and we will *determine* which path of words is yours.' I touched the first scroll and felt a faint warmth rise through my fingers, steady as morning light. The second was cold. The third trembled like a living thing.
determine:0.cnHint: 师尊让我触摸三卷典籍，以此____我适合修炼哪条道路。
determine:0.hook: The third scroll had no title — only a single character that kept changing.
determine:0.line: 'We must *determine* your path before the next moon rises.'

response:0.en: Shen Wujiu called out the word 'still' in the practice hall, and the candle flames bent as one. He turned to me and waited. I opened my mouth and spoke the same word. For a heartbeat, nothing. Then, slowly, every flame straightened — a perfect *response* that surprised even him. I had not expected the hall to feel so alive.
response:0.cnHint: 我念出那个字，整个练功堂的烛火给出了令人惊讶的____。
response:0.hook: From the far wall, a crack of light appeared where no window had ever been.
response:0.line: 'That kind of *response* from the hall — I have not seen it in three years.'

search:0.en: Xiaoxing and I spent the whole morning in a *search* through the sect's inner library, looking for the healing word that Master Qingwu had described only as 'the one that smells like rain.' Shelf after shelf offered nothing. At last, behind a broken jar, I found a strip of bark with two faint characters pressed into it.
search:0.cnHint: 我和小星在藏经阁里____那个"闻起来像雨"的治愈字诀。
search:0.hook: The bark was still damp, as though someone had placed it there only moments before.
search:0.line: 'Our *search* ends here — smell this bark and tell me what you notice.'

due:0.en: The morning lesson was delayed *due* to a thick mist that had rolled in from below the mountain, swallowing the stone steps whole. Master Qingwu stood at the edge and said nothing for a long time. When she finally turned, her expression was not calm — it was careful, the way a person looks when they already know what is coming.
due:0.cnHint: 晨课____浓雾而推迟，师尊站在山边，神情格外慎重。
due:0.hook: The mist carried a low sound, almost like a word being spoken far below.
due:0.line: '*Due* to the mist, we will not practice outside — gather in the inner hall.'

regard:0.en: Shen Wujiu had always been the top disciple, and the younger students *regarded* him with quiet respect. But that afternoon, when his chosen word failed to lift even a feather, the room went very still. He knelt and reset his breath without complaint. In that moment I thought I understood why Master Qingwu had chosen him as our senior.
regard:0.cnHint: 同门们一向____师兄，而那天他失败后的平静举止更让人信服。
regard:0.hook: The fallen feather began to rise on its own, slowly, after he had already left the room.
regard:0.line: 'I *regard* every word I fail as a teacher I have not yet thanked.'

true:0.en: 'Copy this character a hundred times,' Master Qingwu told me, 'and on the last stroke, if your hand does not shake, the word is *true* inside you.' I copied it ninety-nine times without trouble. On the hundredth, my hand stopped halfway through — not from fear, but because something in my chest pulled tight, like a knot being tied.
true:0.cnHint: 师尊说，只有手不颤抖写完最后一笔，这个字才在心中变得____。
true:0.hook: The hundredth character began to glow before the ink had fully dried.
true:0.line: 'A *true* word does not need force — it rises the way breath rises.'

depend:0.en: 'How long until I can fly?' I asked Xiaoxing as we ground dried cloud-petals into powder. She smiled and said it would *depend* on how honestly I practiced, not on how hard I pushed. I wanted to argue, but the little jar of powder in her hands was already lifting off the table, drawn up by nothing more than the soft word she had just breathed.
depend:0.cnHint: 小星告诉我，能否飞翔____于修炼是否诚心，而非蛮力。
depend:0.hook: The powder hung in the air and slowly formed the shape of a bird.
depend:0.line: 'Everything here will *depend* on the honesty you put into each word.'

expensive:0.en: The scroll Shen Wujiu unrolled was sealed with deep-blue thread. 'This formula is the most *expensive* in the sect's keeping,' he said, 'not in silver, but in years — it took three masters a lifetime each to finish it.' I leaned closer and saw that the characters were not written in ink. They were pressed in, as if each one had been placed with great care and great cost.
expensive:0.cnHint: 师兄展示了一卷用心血著成、极为____的古老字诀。
expensive:0.hook: One character near the center was missing — replaced by a single blank space.
expensive:0.line: 'Do not copy it lightly — this is the most *expensive* knowledge we hold.'

explain:0.en: Master Qingwu set a single jade scroll on the stone table before us. 'Before you touch any herb-word,' she said, 'you must *explain* its nature to me — what it heals, what it harms, and why.' I opened my mouth. The scroll began to glow, as if it already knew whether my answer would be true.
explain:0.cnHint: 师尊要求弟子在碰触任何药草字之前，先____它的本质。
explain:0.hook: The scroll's glow deepened, waiting for a truth I had not yet found.
explain:0.line: 'You must *explain* the herb-word's nature before you may hold it.'

examine:0.en: Shen Wujiu laid the five word-tablets in a row on the low bench and told me to *examine* each one with closed eyes, using only my fingertips. 'A true disciple reads with more than sight,' he said. Under my touch the third tablet felt colder than the others — wrong, somehow, like a stone hiding ice.
examine:0.cnHint: 师兄让我用指尖____五块字碑，眼睛必须闭着。
examine:0.hook: The cold tablet pulsed once, and the bench creaked beneath it.
examine:0.line: '*Examine* each tablet with your hands before you judge with your eyes.'

influence:0.en: Master Qingwu warned that the herb-word for wind could *influence* the other words stored nearby, pulling their meaning sideways like a current bends river grass. Xiaoxing and I tied our scroll-cases with double knots that evening. Somewhere above us, the wind-word hummed inside its jar, restless and patient at once.
influence:0.cnHint: 师尊警告说，风之字会____附近储存的其他字的含义。
influence:0.hook: By midnight the hum had grown loud enough to rattle the jar's lid.
influence:0.line: 'That word can *influence* every herb stored beside it — keep them apart.'

argue:0.en: Xiaoxing and I began to *argue* over which word-formula should be written first on the morning paper: the one for stillness or the one for breath. Our voices rose. Master Qingwu did not look up from her brush. She simply wrote both words at once, with two hands, and the paper held them in perfect balance.
argue:0.cnHint: 我和师妹____应该先写哪个字诀，声音越来越大。
argue:0.hook: Master Qingwu's double-brushed paper let out one quiet, warning hiss.
argue:0.line: 'Do not *argue* about order — the words themselves will tell you which comes first.'

pass:0.en: To leave the inner hall each morning, a disciple must *pass* the stone arch without breaking the thin thread of herb-smoke that crosses it at waist height. Shen Wujiu had crossed without trouble for three years. On my first try I held my breath, moved slowly, and felt the smoke curl around me — whole, unbroken.
pass:0.cnHint: 每天早晨，弟子必须____石拱门而不扯断那缕药烟。
pass:0.hook: Behind me, the smoke thread trembled once before going still.
pass:0.line: 'You must *pass* the arch without breaking the smoke — that is today's first lesson.'

serious:0.en: Master Qingwu's expression turned *serious* when she saw that I had copied the healing word with one stroke reversed. 'A wrong stroke does not merely fail,' she said quietly. 'It asks the word to do the opposite of what you intend.' I looked at my copy again. The ink seemed darker than when I had laid it down.
serious:0.cnHint: 师尊看到我写反了一笔时，神情变得____起来。
serious:0.hook: The ink on my paper spread slowly, as though the wrong word were waking.
serious:0.line: 'This is *serious* — a single reversed stroke can turn healing into harm.'

despite:0.en: *Despite* the heavy rain drumming on the roof tiles, Xiaoxing sat at her desk and traced the same word-formula forty times without pause. The candle bent in the draught but did not go out. When I asked if she was tired, she only smiled and laid her brush down for a moment — then picked it up again.
despite:0.cnHint: ____外面大雨倾盆，师妹仍坐在桌前把同一个字诀描了四十遍。
despite:0.hook: On the forty-first trace, her candle flame burned a steady, unnatural blue.
despite:0.line: '*Despite* the storm, the words must be practised — the clouds do not wait for us.'

express:0.en: Master Qingwu told us that a word-formula spoken aloud must *express* only one clear intent, or the spiritual herb would split its answer in two and help no one. I thought of all the times I had wanted two things at once. I wrote the word for clarity on my palm and closed my fist around it. Outside, a single bell rang across the cloud sea.
express:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我们，念出字诀时必须____唯一清晰的意图。
express:0.hook: The bell's echo did not fade — it lingered, shaped like a question.
express:0.line: 'When you speak a formula, *express* one intent only — the herb cannot serve two masters.'

conduct:0.en: Master Qingwu walked slowly around the stone hall, watching each disciple in silence. She said that a disciple's *conduct* — the way one bowed, breathed, and held a brush — was itself a spiritual herb, one that either healed or poisoned the whole sect. I straightened my spine and tried to mean every movement. Outside, a single cloud drifted through the open window and dissolved without a sound.
conduct:0.cnHint: 师尊说，一个弟子的____決定了他能否真正习得云海门的功法。
conduct:0.hook: The cloud left no trace, yet the air smelled of coming rain.
conduct:0.line: 'Your *conduct* in this hall shapes every word you will ever learn.'

reveal:0.en: Shen Wujiu pressed one finger to the center of an old scroll and whispered a word I could not hear. The paper shivered, and layers of ink faded away to *reveal* a second text hidden beneath — golden characters that hummed like bees in a jar. He smiled at my open mouth and rolled the scroll closed again before I could read a single line.
reveal:0.cnHint: 师兄轻触古卷，让它____了藏在普通字句之下的金色秘文。
reveal:0.hook: The golden words had already burned themselves behind my eyes.
reveal:0.line: 'One word, spoken truly, can *reveal* what a hundred lies have buried.'

powerful:0.en: The inner hall held only one object: a small clay bowl filled with still water. Master Qingwu told us it was the most *powerful* thing in the sect. A disciple who spoke the right word above it could call rain to a dry mountain or silence a storm. No one had spoken that word in forty years. The water did not move, yet it watched us.
powerful:0.cnHint: 师尊展示了道场中最____的器物——一只盛着静水的陶碗。
powerful:0.hook: The water's surface held a reflection of a sky none of us could see.
powerful:0.line: 'The most *powerful* herb grows in the quietest soil.'

push:0.en: Shen Wujiu set a candle on the table and told me to move the flame using only a spoken word. My first try produced nothing. My second, nothing again. On my third attempt, a small *push* of warm air left my lips with the word, and the flame leaned east like a bowing head. He nodded once, then covered it with his palm. The room was suddenly very dark.
push:0.cnHint: 我终于用一个字产生了微小的____，让烛火向东倾斜。
push:0.hook: In the dark, something else in the room exhaled.
push:0.line: 'Every great journey begins with one small *push* of honest will.'

wonder:0.en: Xiaoxing led me to the archive on my first morning and stood back while I walked between shelves as tall as trees. Each scroll glowed faintly, and the whole room smelled of pine and old rain. I stopped in the middle, full of *wonder* so large it had no edges. She watched me with patient eyes and said nothing, giving the feeling its proper space.
wonder:0.cnHint: 踏入藏经阁的那一刻，我心中充满了无边无际的____。
wonder:0.hook: One scroll at the far end shivered, though no one had touched it.
wonder:0.line: 'Hold that *wonder* close — it is the first word you will ever truly own.'

design:0.en: Master Qingwu showed us the floor of the inner hall for the first time. Someone had used words carved in stone to *design* a pattern that covered every tile: a slow spiral from the door to the center, each ring a different formula. Walking it, she said, was itself a lesson. I stepped onto the first tile and felt the stone hum beneath my heel like a held breath.
design:0.cnHint: 师尊揭开了内殿地板的秘密——有人用石刻的字____出了一条螺旋形的功法之路。
design:0.hook: The hum climbed my leg and settled, uninvited, near my heart.
design:0.line: 'Those who *design* with words must first live inside what they build.'

exercise:0.en: Each dawn, before the clouds below turned gold, we would *exercise* the five breath-words in sequence: one to steady the body, one to open the mind, one to call water, one to call wind, and one whose meaning no new disciple yet knew. I practiced the first four until my voice was smooth and even. On the fifth, my mouth formed the shape — and something answered from below the clouds.
exercise:0.cnHint: 每天黎明，我们都会依次____五个呼吸字诀，但第五个字诀的回应让我心生疑惑。
exercise:0.hook: The answer from below the clouds did not sound like an echo.
exercise:0.line: '*Exercise* these words daily — they grow stronger each time you mean them.'

space:0.en: The study room held twelve disciples, but Master Qingwu left one cushion empty between each student. She said that a word, like a seed, needs *space* around it to grow roots before it grows wings. I sat with an empty cushion on either side and noticed how clearly I could hear my own breathing. Then, from the empty cushion to my right, came the faint scent of a herb I had never seen.
space:0.cnHint: 师尊在每位弟子之间留出一个____，说这样才能让字诀真正生根。
space:0.hook: The herb-scent had no source, and it was getting stronger.

career:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a long scroll across the stone table. 'Every disciple who enters this hall must choose a path,' she said quietly. 'Healing, flying, or fighting — your *career* in the Sect begins with that single choice.' I pressed my palm to the paper. The ink trembled like a living thing.
career:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，在云海宗的____从一张卷轴上的选择开始。
career:0.hook: The ink moved on its own, circling one word before I touched it.
career:0.line: 'Your *career* here will outlast the mountain beneath your feet.'

medium:0.en: Shen Wujiu placed three objects before me: a feather, a stone, and a hollow reed. 'Each word-herb needs a *medium* to carry its power,' he explained. 'The wrong vessel and the formula fades before it blooms.' I reached for the reed. It hummed against my fingers like a held breath.
medium:0.cnHint: 师兄向我解释，每种词草都需要一种____来传递它的力量。
medium:0.hook: The stone rolled off the table by itself and did not fall.
medium:0.line: 'Without the right *medium*, even the strongest word dies in your hand.'

office:0.en: Master Qingwu's private *office* sat at the peak of the inner hall, its single window open to a wall of white cloud. Rows of sealed jars lined the shelves — each one holding a word too dangerous to speak aloud. She handed me a broom. 'Sweeping is also study,' she said.
office:0.cnHint: 师尊的____位于内堂最高处，我第一次独自踏入那个地方。
office:0.hook: One jar on the highest shelf was breathing.
office:0.line: 'No one enters my *office* without first learning silence.'

culture:0.en: Xiaoxing spread the old wall map between us on the floor. 'The Cloud Sea Sect did not grow from rules,' she said. 'It grew from *culture* — from every disciple who wrote a word and passed it forward.' The painted mountains seemed to shift as she spoke, as if they remembered.
culture:0.cnHint: 师妹解释说，云海宗的____是由一代代弟子传承下来的。
culture:0.hook: At the map's edge, a mountain that no one named began to glow.
culture:0.line: 'Our *culture* is not written in stone — it lives inside every word we learn.'

college:0.en: 'This is not an ordinary school,' Shen Wujiu said, guiding me through the Gate of First Mist. 'Any *college* can teach you dates and numbers. Here, words heal wounds and open sky.' I looked up at the floating peaks and understood, in a small and shaking way, that he was right.
college:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，这里和普通的____不同，词语在这里能治愈伤口、开辟天空。
college:0.hook: Behind us, the Gate of First Mist closed without a sound.
college:0.line: 'A common *college* fills your head; this place fills your breath.'

value:0.en: Master Qingwu set a single character on the table between us. It glowed a faint gold. 'Before you learn to use a word,' she said, 'you must understand its *value* — not its price, but its weight in the world.' I stared at the character. It stared back, patient as stone.
value:0.cnHint: 师尊要我在学会使用一个词之前，先明白它的____。
value:0.hook: The gold light dimmed the moment I thought I understood.
value:0.line: 'The *value* of a word is measured by what it costs to speak it truly.'

connection:0.en: Xiaoxing took my wrist gently and pressed it against the root of a word-tree growing through the hall wall. 'Feel that?' she whispered. 'That pulse is the *connection* between the herb and the formula — break it and the word loses all meaning.' A cold ring of light spread from where we touched.
connection:0.cnHint: 师妹帮我感受词草与咒式之间那条看不见的____。
connection:0.hook: The cold ring reached the ceiling and kept going.
connection:0.line: 'Every great formula begins with one honest *connection* between two living things.'

story:0.en: Late in the evening Shen Wujiu sat beside the lamp and told me a *story* about the Sect's founding disciple, who wrote the first word-formula on nothing but cloud and will. 'We retell it every year,' he said softly, 'because the telling itself keeps the word alive.' Outside, the clouds below us turned briefly silver.
story:0.cnHint: 师兄在灯下给我讲了一个关于宗门创立者的____。
story:0.hook: The silver in the clouds below spelled out a name no one had spoken in a hundred years.
story:0.line: 'A *story* told with belief is itself a kind of formula.'

real:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old wood and dried herbs. Master Qingwu unrolled a scroll and pointed to a single word glowing faintly at its centre. 'Many disciples copy this word,' she said, 'but copying is not mastery. Only when you feel its *real* weight in your breath does it become power.' I pressed my fingertip to the page. The glow spread.
real:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，只有真正感受到字的力量，它才能成为修炼的根基。____的含义远超表面。
real:0.hook: The glow reached my wrist and would not stop.
real:0.line: 'Only when you feel its *real* weight does the word awaken.'

talk:0.en: Shen Wujiu sat cross-legged on the stone floor, eyes closed. I had come to ask about the evening lesson, but he raised one hand before I could speak. 'Words used in idle *talk* lose their edge,' he said quietly. 'Save them. Every word you waste is a herb thrown into the wind.' I sat down beside him and said nothing.
talk:0.cnHint: 师兄提醒我，随意的____会消耗字的灵力，修士要懂得沉默的价值。
talk:0.hook: Outside, the wind carried a sound that was almost a word.
talk:0.line: 'Words spent in idle *talk* are herbs thrown to the wind.'

energy:0.en: Xiaoxing showed me how to hold the brush. 'Write slowly,' she said. 'Feel the *energy* rise from your belly before the ink touches the paper.' I tried three times. On the third stroke a faint warmth climbed my arm, and the character on the page lifted slightly off the surface, trembling like a leaf about to fall.
energy:0.cnHint: 师妹教我运笔时先感受丹田升起的____，字迹才能获得灵气。
energy:0.hook: The trembling character cast a shadow that pointed the wrong way.
energy:0.line: 'Feel the *energy* rise from your belly before the brush moves.'

plan:0.en: Master Qingwu spread seven scrolls across the table, one for each day of the first week. 'This is your *plan*,' she said. 'Each day you learn one word. Each word opens one door. Rush ahead and all the doors stay shut.' I studied the order she had chosen and noticed the seventh word was left blank.
plan:0.cnHint: 师尊为我制定了一周的学习____，每天一个字，但第七天的字栏是空白的。
plan:0.hook: The blank space on the seventh scroll seemed to breathe.
plan:0.line: 'Follow this *plan* exactly — the order is not chosen by chance.'

bear:0.en: The stone pillar in the centre of the study hall was carved with a hundred characters. Shen Wujiu touched the one at the top. 'A master must *bear* the weight of every word she has ever spoken,' he said. 'They do not leave you. They stay in the body like roots.' I looked at my own hands and wondered how many roots I had already planted.
bear:0.cnHint: 师兄说修士必须____自己说出的每一个字所带来的重量，字语如根，留在体内。
bear:0.hook: One carved character near the base had cracked clean through.
bear:0.line: 'A true disciple must *bear* the weight of every word spoken.'

organization:0.en: On the shelf behind Master Qingwu's desk stood row after row of small jars, each labelled in her careful script. 'The *organization* of these herbs took me thirty years,' she said without turning around. 'A word out of place is a herb in the wrong jar. It will heal the wrong thing.' I stepped closer and saw that one jar had no label at all.
organization:0.cnHint: 师尊花了三十年整理药草的____，她说字的排列就如药草，一旦错位便会产生反效果。
organization:0.hook: The unlabelled jar was the only one that moved on its own.
organization:0.line: 'The *organization* of words, like herbs, must be exact.'

opportunity:0.en: 'You will not always have a scroll in front of you,' Master Qingwu said, closing the lesson book. 'Every moment of silence is an *opportunity* to listen for words the mountain is already speaking.' I stood still and for the first time heard a low hum rising through the floor, steady and patient, like something waiting to be named.
opportunity:0.cnHint: 师尊说，每一刻的安静都是倾听山语的____，我第一次听到了地板下稳定的低鸣。
opportunity:0.hook: The hum rose one tone higher and then went silent.
opportunity:0.line: 'Every quiet moment is an *opportunity* the mountain offers you.'

professor:0.en: Shen Wujiu smiled when I called Master Qingwu a teacher. 'She is more than that,' he said. 'In the old sect records she holds the title of *professor* of living words — the only one still alive who can write a word that breathes on its own.' I looked back at the scroll she had given me and noticed, for the first time, that it was rising and falling very slightly.
professor:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，师尊在古老宗门典籍中拥有活字____的称号，是唯一仍在世的活字书写者。
professor:0.hook: The scroll rose and fell like a sleeping chest.
professor:0.line: 'She holds the title of *professor* of living words in the old records.'

sign:0.en: The study hall smelled of old ink and dried herbs. Master Qingwu laid seven word-scrolls across the stone table and asked me to read each one aloud. My voice was steady for six, but at the seventh, the candle flame bent sideways — a clear *sign* that the word held power I had not yet earned. I set the scroll down with care.
sign:0.cnHint: 师尊让我诵读七卷符文，第七卷的烛焰弯曲，是一个____，说明此字我尚未驾驭。
sign:0.hook: The bent flame had not straightened by morning.
sign:0.line: 'That *sign* means the word is still beyond you,' said Master Qingwu.

feeling:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a small clay bowl filled with pale liquid distilled from the word 'calm.' He told me to drink slowly and notice what changed inside. A quiet warmth spread from my chest outward, and I understood that a word, fully absorbed, becomes a *feeling* before it becomes a skill. I placed the empty bowl on the shelf.
feeling:0.cnHint: 师兄让我饮下由'静'字炼成的药液，我领悟到文字在成为技艺之前，先成为一种____。
feeling:0.hook: Outside, the clouds below the mountain shifted without wind.
feeling:0.line: 'A word must first become a *feeling* inside you,' said Shen Wujiu.

professional:0.en: Master Qingwu corrected the angle of my brush for the third time that morning. She said that anyone could copy a word, but a *professional* cultivator shapes each stroke with breath and intent, so the ink itself carries meaning. I steadied my wrist and tried again. The character I drew this time glowed faintly before fading.
professional:0.cnHint: 师尊说，一位____的修炼者落笔时需注入气息与意念，我第三次重写，字迹竟微微发光。
professional:0.hook: The glow lasted three heartbeats longer than it should have.
professional:0.line: 'A *professional* cultivator puts intent into every stroke,' said Master Qingwu.

behind:0.en: The inner library had two rooms. Xiaoxing led me through the first, past rows of common word-scrolls, and stopped at a plain wooden door. She whispered that the rarest formulas were kept *behind* that door, sealed until a disciple proved worthy. I pressed my palm flat against the cold wood and felt a faint pulse, like a slow breath.
behind:0.cnHint: 小星带我走过内库前室，告诉我最珍贵的符文就锁在那扇门____，要等弟子证明自己才能开启。
behind:0.hook: The pulse through the wood beat once more, then went still.
behind:0.line: 'The oldest words are kept *behind* that door,' Xiaoxing said softly.

government:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a wide map showing all the floating mountains in the region. She explained that the Cloud Sea Sect held no land below the clouds, and so it had no part in the *government* of the valley towns. Our power came from words alone, not from law or coin. She rolled the map back up before I could study it fully.
government:0.cnHint: 师尊展示地图，说明云海宗不参与山下谷镇的____，宗门的力量只源于文字，不依赖律法或财富。
government:0.hook: One mountain on the map had no name marked beside it.
government:0.line: 'We take no part in the *government* of those below,' said Master Qingwu.

growth:0.en: Xiaoxing showed me her practice journal, its pages filled with the same word written hundreds of times, each attempt slightly stronger than the last. She said that in cultivation, *growth* never comes all at once — it arrives in small, quiet layers, the way a tree adds rings in the dark. I opened my own blank journal and wrote the first word of my training.
growth:0.cnHint: 小星让我看她的练习册，说修炼中的____从不一蹴而就，而是像树木在暗中悄悄增添年轮。
growth:0.hook: My first written word left a faint scorch mark on the page.
growth:0.line: 'True *growth* in this art comes slowly, like rings inside a tree,' Xiaoxing said.

negative:0.en: Shen Wujiu warned me that some words carry a *negative* charge, pulling energy inward rather than sending it out. Used without care, they could dim a cultivator's spirit for days. He pointed to three characters near the bottom of my practice list and circled them in red. I made a note to approach those words last, and only with a full night's rest behind me.
negative:0.cnHint: 师兄警告我，某些文字带有____能量，会向内吸收力量，他用红笔圈出练习册里三个危险的字。
negative:0.hook: One of the three circled words seemed darker than the ink around it.
negative:0.line: 'Those three carry a *negative* charge — learn them last,' Shen Wujiu warned.

potential:0.en: Master Qingwu read my first week of practice scrolls in silence, her eyes moving without expression. At last she set them down and said that she saw clear *potential* in the way I heard a word before I wrote it — most new disciples did the reverse. She did not smile, but her tone was warmer than before. A single white feather drifted down from the ceiling and landed on my scroll.
potential:0.cnHint: 师尊批阅我第一周的练习卷后，说她看出我有____——因为我先听见文字再落笔，多数新弟子反其道而行。
potential:0.hook: No bird lived in that study hall, and the ceiling was bare stone.
potential:0.line: 'Your habit of listening first shows real *potential*,' said Master Qingwu.

force:0.en: Inside the archive hall, rows of jade slips glowed faintly in the dark. Master Qingwu placed one in my hands and said I must never *force* a spiritual formula into my meridians before I understood its root. 'The herb bends to knowledge, not to will,' she warned.
force:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊告诫弟子，不可用____将灵诀压入经脉。
force:0.hook: A crack ran through the jade slip as she spoke.
force:0.line: 'Never *force* a formula upon your body before your mind is ready.'

importance:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread a worn scroll across the stone table, pointing to a diagram of cloud-root herbs. 'Most disciples ignore this chapter,' he said quietly. 'But the *importance* of knowing which herbs cancel each other out cannot be measured. One wrong pairing and the formula becomes dust.'
importance:0.cnHint: 师兄向我解释，掌握药草相克之理的____不可忽视。
importance:0.hook: At the bottom of the scroll, a name had been burned away.
importance:0.line: 'The *importance* of this pairing is something no disciple should overlook.'

sell:0.en: Xiaoxing returned from the outer market with an empty basket and a pale face. Every rare cloud-petal herb had been taken off the shelves that morning. 'It was not a *sell*-out from demand,' she whispered. 'Someone bought them all before dawn to keep others from healing.'
sell:0.cnHint: 小星从市集回来，发现所有珍稀草药已被____一空。
sell:0.hook: She set the empty basket down, and a single black feather fell out.
sell:0.line: 'Every last cloud-petal was gone — a sudden *sell*-out before sunrise.'

replace:0.en: Master Qingwu stood before the broken formation stone in the inner hall, her sleeve brushing its fractured edge. 'We cannot simply *replace* a foundation stone,' she said softly. 'Each one holds years of gathered breath. A new stone is empty — it must be taught all over again.'
replace:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊说明，损毁的阵基石无法轻易被____。
replace:0.hook: The hall grew colder the moment the stone was touched.
replace:0.line: 'To *replace* this stone is easy; to restore its memory is not.'

approach:0.en: Shen Wujiu circled the worktable three times before touching a single herb. 'The *approach* matters as much as the formula itself,' he told me. 'If you enter a preparation with a hurried mind, the herbs sense it. They will give you only their surface, not their depth.'
approach:0.cnHint: 师兄向我讲解，炼制灵草时的____与配方本身同等重要。
approach:0.hook: One herb on the table trembled, though no wind had entered.
approach:0.line: 'Your *approach* to the herbs will shape everything that follows.'

engage:0.en: Master Qingwu asked me to sit across from a glowing formula disc and simply observe it for one full hour. 'Do not copy it yet,' she said. 'Learn to *engage* with its pattern the way you would listen to rain — fully present, asking nothing.' An hour felt like a breath.
engage:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊要求我先____灵纹阵盘的规律，而非急于抄录。
engage:0.hook: When the hour ended, the disc had changed its shape.
engage:0.line: '*Engage* with the pattern first; copying before listening is no learning at all.'

ensure:0.en: Before leaving the herb room each evening, Xiaoxing checked every seal on every jar twice. 'Cloud-root fades fast once the air touches it,' she explained. 'We must *ensure* the lids hold or three days of work dissolves overnight.' Her fingers moved with quiet, steady certainty.
ensure:0.cnHint: 小星每晚仔细检查封口，以____云根草的药效不会散失。
ensure:0.hook: That night, one jar was found open with nothing inside.
ensure:0.line: 'We *ensure* every seal holds, or our effort means nothing by morning.'

limit:0.en: Shen Wujiu warned me that each disciple's inner cloud-pool had a natural *limit* — a ceiling of spiritual energy the body could hold without harm. 'Push past it once and you grow stronger,' he said, his voice dropping. 'Push past it twice and you begin to hollow out from within.'
limit:0.cnHint: 师兄提醒我，内在云池的____一旦被突破两次，将有损根基。
limit:0.hook: He rolled up his sleeve, and I saw a ring of pale marks.
limit:0.line: 'Every cloud-pool has a *limit*, and the body remembers every time you cross it.'

save:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old ink and dried roots. Master Qingwu placed a worn scroll before me and said nothing. I understood: every word I learned here would *save* something — a life, a fading formula, a memory the clouds had nearly swallowed. I copied the first character with a careful hand.
save:0.cnHint: 在内堂，我意识到学会每一个词都能____某些珍贵的东西。
save:0.hook: The candle bent sideways, though no window was open.
save:0.line: 'A single word, learned in time, can *save* what no sword ever could.'

service:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a small iron tag on my first morning. 'Wear this,' he said quietly. 'It marks your *service* to the sect — every meal you carry, every hall you sweep counts as a word offered to the mountain.' I turned the tag over; a faint glow ran along its edge.
service:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，这块铁牌代表我对宗门的____，每一份劳作都被山峰记录在册。
service:0.hook: By nightfall the tag was warm, as if the mountain had noticed me.
service:0.line: 'Your *service* here is never small — the mountain weighs every act.'

note:0.en: Xiaoxing slid a folded paper under my door before the morning bell. Inside was a single *note* — not words but a drawn curve, the shape a brush makes when calling wind. I traced it with one finger and felt the air in the room tilt, just slightly, toward the window.
note:0.cnHint: 小星在纸上留了一个____，那是一个召唤风的笔画形状。
note:0.hook: Outside, a loose leaf rose and hung still, waiting.
note:0.line: 'Copy this *note* exactly — the mountain hears the shape, not the intention.'

probably:0.en: I asked Shen Wujiu how long it would take to speak the first flying word correctly. He thought for a moment, watching the clouds below the terrace. 'Three months if you are careful,' he said. 'You will *probably* make the mistake I made — rushing the last stroke.' He did not say what happened when he rushed it.
probably:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，我____会犯他当年犯过的错误，但没有说那个错误的后果。
probably:0.hook: A distant rumble rolled up from the cloud sea, low and patient.
probably:0.line: 'You will *probably* feel the word resist you — that is the moment to slow down.'

strategy:0.en: Master Qingwu spread twelve word-tablets across the stone table and asked me to choose three. 'Your *strategy* matters more than your effort,' she said. 'A disciple who picks healing words first builds a foundation; one who picks fighting words first builds a wall with no floor.' I stared at the tablets for a long time.
strategy:0.cnHint: 师尊说，选择哪三个词片来修炼，体现的是你的____，而非你的努力。
strategy:0.hook: One tablet near the edge glowed faintly, as if already chosen.
strategy:0.line: 'Without a clear *strategy*, even the brightest talent will circle the same peak forever.'

building:0.en: The archive stood at the mountain's heart — a *building* made of pale stone that had grown, over centuries, into the cliff face itself. Shen Wujiu told me the walls held every word the sect had ever mastered. I pressed one hand flat against the stone and felt a low hum travel up my arm.
building:0.cnHint: 宗门档案馆是一座融入山壁的____，据说墙壁里储存着历代掌握的所有词语。
building:0.hook: A crack I had not noticed before ran from floor to ceiling, fresh and thin.
building:0.line: 'This *building* remembers every word ever spoken inside it — choose yours with care.'

community:0.en: On the seventh day, all new disciples gathered in the open courtyard. Master Qingwu looked at each of us in turn. 'You are no longer alone in your learning,' she said. 'A *community* of words is stronger than any single voice — your meanings will hold each other up when the wind tests them.' Clouds drifted silently beneath our feet.
community:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我们，作为一个____共同修炼，我们的词语之力将会相互支撑。
community:0.hook: At that moment every disciple's practice scroll glowed the same faint gold.
community:0.line: 'A *community* that shares its words can move a mountain no single disciple could shift.'

internet:0.en: An elder from a far peak visited the archive and spoke of a web of word-paths linking all the floating mountains — a living *internet* of meaning that carried knowledge from summit to summit without any scroll or messenger. Xiaoxing leaned close and whispered, 'That web once went silent for a whole season. Nobody knows why.'
internet:0.cnHint: 一位长老描述了连接所有浮山的意义之网——一张活的____，静默过整整一季。
internet:0.hook: That night, my own practice scroll received a message no one had sent.
internet:0.line: 'The sect's *internet* of paths is older than any living master — and it still has secrets.'

perhaps:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old pine and dried cloud-moss. Master Qingwu set a glowing scroll before me and said nothing for a long moment. *Perhaps* this silence was itself the first lesson — a test of whether I could sit still while the mountain breathed around me. I held my hands in my lap and waited. Outside, wind moved through the bell tower.
perhaps:0.cnHint: 师尊将发光的卷轴放在我面前，沉默良久，而我只能静静等待____这份沉默本身就是第一课。
perhaps:0.hook: Then the scroll began to unroll on its own.
perhaps:0.line: '*Perhaps* stillness is the first word any disciple must learn,' said Master Qingwu.

video:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread a thin sheet of crystal on the low table. 'This is a *video* stone,' he said — a record-crystal that could hold moving images of a master's hand-form, so disciples who missed a live lesson could still study the motion. I watched my own clumsy fingers reflected in its dark surface. Somewhere deeper in the sect, a gong rang once.
video:0.cnHint: 师兄向我展示一块能储存动态影像的水晶石，称之为____石，让我可以反复观看师尊的手法。
video:0.hook: In the crystal's reflection, a third figure stood behind me.
video:0.line: 'A *video* stone holds a master's form — watch it until your hands remember,' said Shen Wujiu.

prevent:0.en: The candle flame bent sharply to the left, though no window was open. Xiaoxing pressed a paper seal across the door frame and explained that the seal was meant to *prevent* rogue wind-words from drifting in during our study hour — stray syllables could tangle with a beginner's practice and cause the herb-light to flare. I believed her. My palms were already warm.
prevent:0.cnHint: 小星在门框上贴了一张符，说是为了____流浪的风咒在我们练习时飘入室内。
prevent:0.hook: The seal cracked down the middle before she finished speaking.
prevent:0.line: 'We use this seal to *prevent* wild words from entering the hall,' said Xiaoxing.

source:0.en: Master Qingwu traced a single character in the air and it hung there, faintly gold. 'Every word-herb has a *source*,' she said, 'a root deep in the mountain's memory. Find that root and the word will grow for you. Ignore it and the word will wither on your tongue.' The golden character pulsed once, then dissolved into smoke that smelled of rain.
source:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，每一个字草都有其____——藏于山脉记忆深处的根，必须找到它，字才能生长。
source:0.hook: The smoke drifted upward and spelled a warning I could not yet read.
source:0.line: 'Tell me the *source* of this word and you will never forget its power,' said Master Qingwu.

available:0.en: I searched every shelf in the preparation room for the text on cloud-breath forms, but Shen Wujiu shook his head. 'That scroll is not *available* to first-year disciples,' he said quietly, not unkind. 'Master Qingwu keeps it sealed until the third-moon trial.' I nodded and chose a simpler volume. Its pages felt warmer than they should.
available:0.cnHint: 我在备药室找一本关于云息法的书，师兄告诉我那卷轴对一年级弟子还不____，要等到三月试验之后。
available:0.hook: The sealed scroll on the high shelf trembled as I turned to leave.
available:0.line: 'That text is not *available* to you yet — but your time will come,' said Shen Wujiu.

customer:0.en: Once a month, a trader climbed the lower path to the sect's herb-gate. Each *customer* who came to buy dried word-seeds had to state, aloud, the common name and the rare name of what they wanted — a small proof they were not buying blindly. I stood at the gate beside Xiaoxing and listened. The trader's voice was careful, almost reverent.
customer:0.cnHint: 每月都有商人来药门购买字草种子，每位____必须大声说出所购草药的俗名与雅名，以示非盲目购买。
customer:0.hook: The last item the trader named was not on any shelf we knew.
customer:0.line: 'Every *customer* here must speak the herb's true name before we trade,' said Xiaoxing.

language:0.en: 'Words are not decoration,' Master Qingwu said, holding a single dried leaf up to the lamp. 'The *language* of this sect is alive — each syllable carries weight, heat, or cold. Speak carelessly and the mountain will answer carelessly.' I copied the phrase into my record-book three times. My brushstrokes were unsteady, but by the third line they held still.
language:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，宗门的____是活的，每个音节都承载着重量或冷热，不可随意开口。
language:0.hook: My third line of brushwork began to glow faint green on its own.
language:0.line: 'The *language* of cloud and herb is never just sound — it is intention,' said Master Qingwu.

test:0.en: Shen Wujiu set three small jars on the table and folded his arms. 'This is a *test* of your nose, not your memory,' he said. Each jar held a different ground word-herb; I had to name all three by scent alone, without lifting the lids. I closed my eyes. Two came to me easily. The third smelled like thunder, and I had no name for thunder yet.
test:0.cnHint: 师兄把三个小罐放在桌上，说这是一次____，要我仅凭气味说出每种字草的名字，不许掀开盖子。
test:0.hook: The third jar began to hum softly the longer I hesitated.
test:0.line: 'A simple *test* — name what you smell, and trust your instinct,' said Shen Wujiu.

seek:0.en: The library hall smelled of old wood and dried ink. I ran my fingers along shelf after shelf, *seeking* the one scroll that held the word for mist-walking. Shen Wujiu had told me it glowed faintly blue at the spine. I found nothing — yet when I turned to leave, every candle in the hall went out at once.
seek:0.cnHint: 我在藏书阁里____那卷记载雾行术的古籍，却在离开时遭遇了异象。
seek:0.hook: In the sudden dark, something on the highest shelf began to hum.
seek:0.line: '*Seek* the blue spine first — all other scrolls will mislead you,' Shen Wujiu warned.

exist:0.en: Master Qingwu set a clay bowl of water before me and said nothing. I stared until my eyes ached. Then I saw it: a tiny word, written in light, just below the surface. Words could *exist* inside still water — nobody had told me that. I reached one finger toward it, and the water rippled into the shape of a closed eye.
exist:0.cnHint: 我第一次发现，灵文竟然能____于静水之中，师尊却似乎早已知晓。
exist:0.hook: The eye in the water blinked once, then was still.
exist:0.line: 'A word can *exist* in water, in stone, in breath — learn to look,' said Master Qingwu.

supply:0.en: Xiaoxing spread the lesson tokens across the low table, counting under her breath. Our weekly *supply* of practice words had come — twelve tokens, each carved from pale cloud-wood. But she held the last one up and frowned. It was cracked clean through, and the word carved on it had already faded to nothing.
supply:0.cnHint: 小星清点本周练习灵文的____，发现最后一枚令牌已经碎裂且字迹消失。
supply:0.hook: A cracked token had never appeared in the Sect's records — not once in three hundred years.
supply:0.line: 'Our *supply* this week is twelve tokens, but one of them is already dead,' Xiaoxing murmured.

visit:0.en: It was the third dawn of my training when Master Qingwu made her first *visit* to my practice room. She stood in the doorway, said nothing, and watched me copy the word for 'wind' seventeen times. On the eighteenth stroke, my brush stopped moving on its own. The ink rose from the page in a thin, curling line of smoke.
visit:0.cnHint: 师尊第一次____我的练习室，恰好目睹了我书写灵文时发生的奇异一幕。
visit:0.hook: The smoke twisted into an arrow and pointed toward the sealed inner gate.
visit:0.line: 'This *visit* will be my only one — after this, the room judges you alone,' said Master Qingwu.

worry:0.en: Shen Wujiu sat beside me after the evening bell, turning a lesson token in his hand. He said his only *worry* was not the hard words or the long hours — it was the silence a word made just before it worked. That silence, he said, could swallow a careless mind whole. Outside, the wind dropped to nothing, as if to prove him right.
worry:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，他唯一的____不是苦练，而是灵文生效前那一瞬间的寂静。
worry:0.hook: The silence that followed his words lasted just a little too long.
worry:0.line: 'My only *worry* is the moment before the word takes hold,' Shen Wujiu said quietly.

adapt:0.en: The morning drill required me to write the same word on paper, on bark, and then on air with a wet finger. My hand knew the strokes, but I had to *adapt* the pressure each time — too firm on air and the word dissolved, too light on bark and it never formed. Xiaoxing watched from across the room; her own word hung perfect and still, glowing like a lantern.
adapt:0.cnHint: 晨练要求我在不同介质上书写同一灵文，必须不断____力道，而小星的字已悬在空中发光。
adapt:0.hook: When I finally held my air-word steady, every other light in the room dimmed.
adapt:0.line: 'You must *adapt* your touch to whatever holds the word,' Xiaoxing said, not unkindly.

bit:0.en: Master Qingwu taught us that power came not from long words but from small ones. A single *bit* of the right syllable, placed at the end of a spoken formula, could turn a healing word into a warding one. I tried it once, quietly, over my ink stone. The stone cracked down the center — clean, slow, and perfectly silent.
bit:0.cnHint: 师尊说，在咒语末尾加上正确的一____音节，便能改变整个灵文的效果，我亲手验证了这一点。
bit:0.hook: Inside each half of the cracked stone, a new word had already begun to form.
bit:0.line: 'One small *bit* of sound at the end changes everything — do not forget it,' Master Qingwu said.

check:0.en: Before any disciple could leave the hall, Shen Wujiu would *check* each practice scroll against the master copy pinned to the north wall. He held mine up to the window light, compared it stroke by stroke, and then set it down without a word. That silence meant something — it always did. On the master copy, one character had begun to bleed slow red ink.
check:0.cnHint: 师兄逐一____弟子的练习卷轴，看完我的之后沉默不语，而此时墙上的母本开始渗出红色墨迹。
check:0.hook: Red ink on the master copy had not been seen since the Sect's last great crisis.
check:0.line: 'I *check* every scroll before sunset — a missed stroke here costs more than you know,' said Shen Wujiu.

effective:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a small leaf pressed flat between two pages. 'Say the word on this leaf three times,' he said. I did. The bruise on my wrist faded like ink washed by rain. 'Words are only *effective*,' he added quietly, 'when you believe them.' A single candle in the corner bent its flame toward me.
effective:0.cnHint: 师兄给我一片叶子，让我念上面的词三遍，瘀伤消散了，他说这词只有在你相信时才____。
effective:0.hook: The candle flame had been perfectly still all evening — until now.
effective:0.line: 'A word is only *effective* when your breath carries no doubt.'

fear:0.en: I stood alone in the archive room, holding a scroll I could not read. The characters shifted each time my eyes moved. Master Qingwu had warned me: some words feed on *fear*. I steadied my breath, the way she taught, and the characters slowed. But one — one kept moving, tracing a shape I did not want to name.
fear:0.cnHint: 我独自站在藏经室，手持一卷无法读懂的卷轴，师尊曾警告说有些字以____为食。
fear:0.hook: The shape it traced looked exactly like my own name.
fear:0.line: '*Fear* is just a word that has learned to breathe on its own.'

hit:0.en: Xiaoxing tapped the ink stone gently until the brush *hit* the exact center of the page. 'Location matters,' she told me, eyes bright. 'A healing word placed at the edge of the paper loses half its strength.' She slid the page toward me to try. The ink, still wet, glowed faintly gold before it dried.
hit:0.cnHint: 师妹轻轻敲击砚台，让笔____纸张正中央，说位置决定药力强弱。
hit:0.hook: The gold glow returned, though neither of us had touched the page.
hit:0.line: 'Make sure the first stroke *hits* the center, or the word loses its heart.'

assume:0.en: I made the mistake every new disciple makes: I read the word aloud before studying its meaning. Shen Wujiu found me sitting on the floor, dizzy. 'You *assumed* it was a simple greeting word,' he said, not unkindly. 'It was a word for summoning wind.' Above the sect hall, the wind chimes rang on a still afternoon.
assume:0.cnHint: 我在没弄清含义前就念出了那个词，师兄说我____那只是个普通问候语，其实它是唤风之词。
assume:0.hook: The wind chimes had been removed from the hall two winters ago.
assume:0.line: 'Never *assume* a word is harmless before you know its root.'

generally:0.en: Master Qingwu walked slowly between the rows of writing desks, hands behind her back. '*Generally*,' she said, her voice even and low, 'a student takes three months to write the first living word. You have been here three weeks.' She stopped behind my desk. I did not look up. The ink in my brush was still warm.
generally:0.cnHint: 师尊在书桌间缓步走动，说____来说学生需要三个月才能写出第一个活字，而我只来了三周。
generally:0.hook: She had not yet looked at what I had written.
generally:0.line: '*Generally*, the brush knows before the student does — watch it.'

interaction:0.en: Xiaoxing spread two word-leaves flat on the stone floor, keeping them a hand's width apart. 'Never let opposing words touch,' she warned. 'The *interaction* between a fire word and a water word can crack the stone beneath.' I nodded, moving my sleeve back carefully. Deep in the mountain, something hummed, low and steady.
interaction:0.cnHint: 师妹将两片字叶分开摆放，说两个对立词语之间的____会震裂石头。
interaction:0.hook: The humming in the mountain grew one note louder as I leaned closer.
interaction:0.line: 'The *interaction* between these two words is older than the mountain we stand on.'

top:0.en: The archive room held ten thousand scrolls, and the oldest were kept at the very *top*, on shelves that disappeared into shadow. Shen Wujiu told me never to climb there alone. I looked up anyway, counting the shelves. On the highest one, something faintly glowed — not a scroll, but a single loose page, trembling in no wind.
top:0.cnHint: 藏经室最____层的架子消失在阴影中，师兄叮嘱我不要独自攀爬，但我抬头望去，看到一页纸在无风中颤动。
top:0.hook: The glow pulsed once, as if it had noticed me looking.
top:0.line: 'The words at the *top* are not locked away because they are rare — they are locked away because they are awake.'

easily:0.en: The study hall was warm with lamp light. Master Qingwu laid seven herb-words on the stone table, their glow faint but steady. 'A careless disciple can *easily* mistake the word for silence and the word for stillness,' she said. I stared at the two glowing signs, searching for a difference I could not yet see.
easily:0.cnHint: 师尊告诫我，两个相似的字草很____被混淆，我盯着它们却看不出差异。
easily:0.hook: Then one sign flickered — and the other went dark.
easily:0.line: 'A tired mind can *easily* call the wrong word and bring the wrong wind.'

protect:0.en: Shen Wujiu pressed a pale blue word-seal into my palm before the night lesson began. 'Wear it,' he said quietly. 'This one will *protect* your breath from the cold herb-smoke that fills the inner hall.' I closed my fingers around it; it hummed like a small, calm heart against my skin.
protect:0.cnHint: 师兄给了我一个字印，说它能____我不受内堂草烟侵扰。
protect:0.hook: A thin crack ran through the seal before I even stepped inside.
protect:0.line: 'Every new disciple needs something to *protect* them on the first cold night.'

advantage:0.en: Master Qingwu drew two word-paths on the slate board: one short and bright, one long and dim. 'Knowing the short path is an *advantage*,' she said, 'but only if your breath is steady enough to walk it.' I copied both paths, unsure which one I would be brave enough to choose.
advantage:0.cnHint: 师尊说掌握捷径是一种____，但需要足够平稳的气息才能驾驭。
advantage:0.hook: That night the short path on my paper began to glow on its own.
advantage:0.line: 'Speed is only an *advantage* when the word beneath your feet is solid.'

break:0.en: The silence in the reading room was total until I pressed the wrong herb-seal too hard against the page. There was a soft crack — a *break* in the formula — and the warm amber light that filled the room vanished all at once. I sat in darkness, holding two pieces of what had been one word.
break:0.cnHint: 我用力过猛，导致字印出现了____，室内的光瞬间熄灭。
break:0.hook: In the dark, something outside the window began to breathe.
break:0.line: 'One *break* in the seal is enough to let the cold thought in.'

conclude:0.en: After I read the three test-words aloud, Master Qingwu was quiet for a long moment. Then she said: 'From your tone and your timing, I *conclude* that you have been practicing in secret, past the bell.' She did not seem angry. She seemed almost pleased, which felt stranger than any punishment.
conclude:0.cnHint: 师尊通过我的语气和节奏____我一直在私下练习，我不知道她是否会责罚我。
conclude:0.hook: She then reached for a scroll I had never seen before.
conclude:0.line: 'I *conclude* that you are further along than you have admitted.'

figure:0.en: On the inner wall of the study hall hung an old painted *figure*: a disciple mid-step, one foot over a cloud, both hands raised around a circle of bright words. No one had told me who it was. Xiaoxing whispered that the face had been rubbed out on purpose, long before either of us arrived.
figure:0.cnHint: 内堂墙上挂着一幅古老的____，画中弟子的脸被人刻意抹去了。
figure:0.hook: Tonight, for the first time, the painted hands seemed to move.
figure:0.line: 'That *figure* on the wall was a warning, not a decoration.'

fit:0.en: Xiaoxing handed me a small wooden word-frame, carved with border signs that glowed a soft green. 'Try it,' she said. I placed my practice seal inside — it did not *fit*. The frame was cut for someone with a stronger foundation, and the seal rattled loosely like a stone in a bowl too wide.
fit:0.cnHint: 小星给我一个字框，但我的字印放进去不____，框是为底子更深的人刻的。
fit:0.hook: The frame then closed on its own, trapping the seal inside.
fit:0.line: 'If it does not *fit* your hand now, that is only a matter of time.'

particular:0.en: Master Qingwu asked each of us to choose one herb-word from the shelf for the evening task. Most disciples reached quickly. I stood still, moving my hand slowly past each glowing jar. There was one *particular* word at the far end that pulled at something behind my ribs, though I could not name the feeling.
particular:0.cnHint: 师尊让我们各选一个字草，我被最末端一个____的字草莫名吸引。
particular:0.hook: When I finally lifted that jar, the room fell completely silent.
particular:0.line: 'You were drawn to that *particular* word — that is not an accident.'

consequence:0.en: The training hall smelled of old wood and dried herbs. Master Qingwu set a single leaf on the stone table and said nothing for a long moment. 'Every word you speak carries a *consequence*,' she said at last. 'Speak a healing word carelessly, and the cloud beneath your feet may vanish.' I stared at the leaf and felt the weight of her silence settle into my bones.
consequence:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，每一个字都有其____，说错了脚下的云就会消散。
consequence:0.hook: Somewhere below, a disciple screamed — then went very quiet.
consequence:0.line: 'Every word you speak carries a *consequence*, so choose each one as if your life depends on it.'

realize:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a scroll and watched me read. The characters swam before my eyes like fish in still water. Then, slowly, the meaning rose to the surface and I began to *realize* that each stroke was not ink but compressed wind. My hand trembled. He gave a small, satisfied nod and turned back to his own practice without a word.
realize:0.cnHint: 我慢慢____，卷轴上的每一笔都不是墨水，而是凝缩的风。
realize:0.hook: The scroll grew warm in my grip, and a faint crack ran across its seal.
realize:0.line: 'Did you *realize* yet that every stroke here holds a living breath?'

mostly:0.en: The inner library was *mostly* silence and pale light. Rows of jade slips lined the curved walls, each one humming at a pitch too low for ordinary ears. Xiaoxing sat cross-legged in the center, lips moving without sound. I chose a slip from the lowest shelf, pressed it to my temple, and felt a cold river pour through my thoughts.
mostly:0.cnHint: 内藏室____是沉默和淡光，师妹正盘坐其中默默诵读。
mostly:0.hook: One slip at the far end pulsed red, once, then fell still.
mostly:0.line: 'The lower shelves are *mostly* safe — stay away from the red ones near the top.'

exactly:0.en: Master Qingwu drew the word for 'wind' in the air with two fingers. 'Place the breath *exactly* here,' she said, touching the space between her brows, 'not a hair higher, not a hair lower.' I tried. A small gust circled the room and died. She drew the character again, and this time the candles bent in perfect unison, bowing like students before a lesson.
exactly:0.cnHint: 师尊说，气息要____放在这个位置，差一分都不行。
exactly:0.hook: A candle at the end of the row did not bow — it went out.
exactly:0.line: 'Place your breath *exactly* here, and the word will answer you.'

vary:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread twelve stones across the study table, each carved with the same character for 'water.' 'Read them aloud,' he said. I did. The sound each stone returned was different — some cool, some almost warm. 'The meaning does not *vary*,' he said, 'but the feeling beneath the meaning does. That feeling is what decides whether you heal or harm.'
vary:0.cnHint: 师兄说，字的意思不会____，但字下面的感觉会变，那感觉决定你是治愈还是伤害。
vary:0.hook: The twelfth stone cracked clean in two before I could touch it.
vary:0.line: 'The meaning does not *vary*, but the feeling beneath it decides everything.'

brain:0.en: The meditation room was cool and dim. Xiaoxing pressed a thin ribbon of cloud-silk to my forehead before I sat down. 'It helps the *brain* stay still,' she said softly, 'so the words can move through without catching on your own thoughts.' I closed my eyes. For the first time since arriving at the Sect, the noise inside my head thinned to a single, clean note.
brain:0.cnHint: 师妹说，云丝带能让____保持平静，让字句流过而不被自己的念头绊住。
brain:0.hook: The note held — then split into two, tuned to a key I did not recognize.
brain:0.line: 'When the *brain* is still, the words find their own path through you.'

stress:0.en: Shen Wujiu had me repeat the same line from the healing sutra thirty times. On the thirty-first, he finally said: 'There. Hear where the *stress* falls — on the second breath, not the third. That shift is the difference between closing a wound and opening it further.' I felt the difference in my chest before I heard it in my voice, like a key finding its groove.
stress:0.cnHint: 师兄说，听清楚____落在哪个字上，一个字的差别就是愈合与撕裂伤口的分别。
stress:0.hook: Outside, the mountain shivered, and a thin crack appeared in the lecture hall wall.
stress:0.line: 'Hear where the *stress* falls — that shift is the difference between healing and harm.'

financial:0.en: The Sect's record room smelled of cedar and old ink. A senior disciple explained that every herb-word traded between sects was logged here for balance. 'We are not merchants,' she said, 'but even cultivation has *financial* roots — a sect that cannot sustain itself cannot teach.' I looked at the long columns of debts and gifts and understood that power and provision were never fully separate.
financial:0.cnHint: 师姐解释说，修炼宗门也有____根基，维持不下去就无法传道。
financial:0.hook: One column near the bottom showed a debt unpaid for a hundred years, marked in red that had not faded.
financial:0.line: 'Even cultivation has *financial* roots — a sect that cannot sustain itself cannot teach.'

fruit:0.en: Inside the Herb Hall, Master Qingwu placed a small, glowing seed on the stone table before me. 'Every word you master,' she said quietly, 'will bear *fruit* in time — a light that can mend a broken wing or calm a storm.' I cupped the seed in both hands, feeling its warmth pulse like a second heartbeat. Outside, the clouds shifted into the shape of an open hand.
fruit:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，每一个掌握的词都会结出____，就像那颗发光的种子。
fruit:0.hook: The seed's glow dimmed — then flared, twice as bright.
fruit:0.line: 'Every word you master will bear *fruit* in time, young disciple.'

waste:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread ten rare word-scrolls across the reading mat, each one humming with stored breath. 'Do not *waste* a single syllable,' he said, tapping the edge of the first scroll. 'Each sound costs a piece of the mountain.' I nodded, hardly daring to breathe, and picked up my brush with careful, trembling fingers. A thin crack ran silently across the inkstone.
waste:0.cnHint: 师兄警告我，不要____任何一个音节，每一个字都来之不易。
waste:0.hook: The crack in the inkstone spread toward my hand.
waste:0.line: 'Do not *waste* a single syllable — each sound costs the mountain.'

learning:0.en: The inner library smelled of pine resin and old cloud-silk. I had been copying word-roots for three hours when Xiaoxing set a cup of warm water beside my brush. 'The elders say *learning* is like filling a jar one drop at a time,' she whispered, glancing at the sealed door at the far end of the room. I smiled, but the sealed door had not been there yesterday.
learning:0.cnHint: 小星提醒我，____如同一滴一滴地注满水罐，需要耐心。
learning:0.hook: The sealed door at the far end had not been there yesterday.
learning:0.line: '*Learning* is like filling a jar — one drop, then another.'

manager:0.en: Master Qingwu introduced Elder Boren as the *manager* of the sect's word-vault, the stone room where every recovered formula was locked away. He bowed without smiling and handed me a thin ledger. 'Sign your name. Nothing enters or leaves without a record.' His brush hovered over a line already marked in red, and the candle between us went out without wind.
manager:0.cnHint: 宗门字库有一位____，他要求我在账册上签名，一切出入都要留有记录。
manager:0.hook: The candle between us went out without any wind.
manager:0.line: 'As *manager* of the vault, I record every word that enters.'

knowledge:0.en: I found the answer to my first trial not in any scroll, but in the worn grooves of the floor where thousands of disciples had knelt before me. Shen Wujiu crouched beside me, tracing the grooves with one finger. 'That is *knowledge* no teacher can give you,' he said softly. 'It lives in stone and silence.' Above us, a bell rang once, though no hand had touched it.
knowledge:0.cnHint: 我在地板的磨痕中发现了答案，师兄说那是任何老师都无法给予的____。
knowledge:0.hook: The bell above us rang once, though no hand touched it.
knowledge:0.line: 'That kind of *knowledge* lives in stone — no teacher can give it.'

mental:0.en: Three nights without sleep had left my strokes crooked and my voice flat. Master Qingwu studied me from across the mat and said nothing for a long moment. 'The trial ahead is not a test of breath or bone,' she finally said. 'It is a *mental* climb — steep, dark, and yours alone.' She closed her eyes, and a faint silver mist began to rise from the floor around her feet.
mental:0.cnHint: 师尊说，前方的考验不在于体力，而是一场____上的攀登。
mental:0.hook: Silver mist rose from the floor around Master Qingwu's feet.
mental:0.line: 'This trial is a *mental* climb — steep, dark, and yours alone.'

weight:0.en: Xiaoxing handed me the sect's oldest pronunciation stone, a slab no bigger than my palm but dense as iron. My wrist dipped the moment I took it. 'You feel its *weight*,' she said with a small smile, 'because it holds every sound the first disciples ever shaped.' I straightened my arm and held it level. Somewhere below the mountain, the sea of clouds let out a long, low sound.
weight:0.cnHint: 小星递给我一块古老的发音石，我感受到了它的____，因为它承载着无数前辈留下的声音。
weight:0.hook: Below the mountain, the sea of clouds let out a low, steady sound.
weight:0.line: 'You feel its *weight* because it carries every sound they ever shaped.'

academic:0.en: The scroll Master Qingwu unrolled was covered in small, precise characters — a full *academic* record of every word-formula the sect had ever lost and then recovered. 'Read it before dawn,' she said, and left without another word. I lifted the first edge of the scroll, and it was longer than the room. Far above, the peak of our mountain glowed faintly red against the dark sky.
academic:0.cnHint: 师尊展开一卷完整的____记录，要我在天亮前读完，那卷轴却比整个房间还长。
academic:0.hook: The mountain peak above glowed faintly red against the dark sky.

major:0.en: Master Qingwu laid seven scrolls across the stone table. 'Six of these words are simple herbs,' she said quietly. 'But one is a *major* formula — it can lift a mountain or shatter a cloud.' I reached for the brightest scroll without thinking. The room went very still.
major:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，七卷中有一卷是____的咒方，我不假思索地伸手去拿。
major:0.hook: The scroll was warm — far too warm for paper.
major:0.line: 'That one carries a *major* secret, so choose with care.'

communication:0.en: Shen Wujiu pressed his ear to the hollow pine at the centre of our study hall. 'The old trees pass words through their roots,' he told me. 'That is the sect's oldest form of *communication*.' I listened too, and heard something low and slow moving beneath the floor.
communication:0.cnHint: 师兄说树根之间的____是宗门最古老的传讯方式，我侧耳倾听，脚下似有低沉之声。
communication:0.hook: The sound was not moving toward us — it was circling.
communication:0.line: 'Root *communication* never lies, but it rarely speaks plainly.'

market:0.en: Every new moon, the elders opened a small *market* inside the East Pavilion, where disciples traded rare words like merchants trade silk. Xiaoxing held up a single character written on bark and smiled at me. I had nothing left to offer — my pouches were empty.
market:0.cnHint: 每逢新月，弟子们在东阁开____，用珍稀字符以物换物，师妹向我展示一枚树皮字符。
market:0.hook: Then I noticed her eyes were fixed just above my head.
market:0.line: 'At this *market*, even a whisper can be worth a mountain.'

apply:0.en: Xiaoxing showed me how to *apply* a healing word to a wound the way a healer presses a leaf to skin — gently, with full attention, letting the meaning sink in slowly. I tried it on my bruised hand. The ache faded. Then, without warning, the word drifted off my palm and rose toward the ceiling.
apply:0.cnHint: 师妹教我如何将治愈字符____于伤处，我照做后疼痛消退，但那字符却无故飘向屋顶。
apply:0.hook: It stopped at the rafter, glowing — and would not come down.
apply:0.line: '*Apply* it softly — a word forced in will fight back.'

per:0.en: Master Qingwu said each disciple was allowed three words *per* day from the library shelf — no more, because the mind needed rest between each one. I had already taken three when I spotted a fourth glowing faintly at the shelf's far end, pulsing like a second heartbeat.
per:0.cnHint: 师尊规定每人每天____可取三个字符，我已取足三个，却发现书架尽头有第四个在微微发光。
per:0.hook: It was pulsing in time with something inside my chest.
per:0.line: 'Three words *per* day keeps the spirit balanced — do not break that rule.'

treat:0.en: Shen Wujiu brought two bowls of cloud-plum soup to the study room — a rare *treat* given only when a disciple passed their first recitation. He set one bowl before me without a word. Outside, the wind had dropped completely, and the floating mountain felt very far from anything solid.
treat:0.cnHint: 师兄端来两碗云梅汤作为____，无声地放在我面前，窗外的风突然停了。
treat:0.hook: In the stillness, I heard the mountain creak once, slowly.
treat:0.line: 'A small *treat* for your first success — enjoy it while the calm holds.'

creative:0.en: 'Be *creative*,' Master Qingwu said, watching me arrange three word-stones on the floor. 'The formula does not care how you place them, only that you understand why.' I moved the smallest stone to the edge. Light gathered at the gap I had made, thin and sharp as a blade.
creative:0.cnHint: 师尊要我____地摆放三块字石，我将最小的一块挪到边缘，缝隙间聚起细而锐的光。
creative:0.hook: The light was pointing at the door — and the door was opening.
creative:0.line: 'A *creative* mind is the one tool no enemy can take from you.'

perform:0.en: It was my turn to *perform* the Morning Word in front of the full hall. I stood at the lectern, breathed in, and spoke the syllable exactly as I had practiced. Every candle flame leaned toward me at once. The hall was silent for a moment longer than felt natural.
perform:0.cnHint: 轮到我在全堂面前____晨诵，我开口发音，所有烛焰同时朝我倾斜。
perform:0.hook: Then one candle went out — though there was no wind.
perform:0.line: 'You must *perform* each word as if the mountain itself is listening.'

trouble:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old pine and dried herbs. Master Qingwu set down her brush and looked at me without blinking. 'You copied the formula wrong,' she said. 'That kind of *trouble* does not stay small — it grows, like a crack in a bell.' I bowed and rewrote every line until the ink ran true.
trouble:0.cnHint: 师尊警告我，这次抄错法诀带来的____不会自己消失。
trouble:0.hook: Outside, the wind chime rang once — though no wind blew.
trouble:0.line: 'That kind of *trouble* does not stay small — it grows, like a crack in a bell.'

reflect:0.en: I knelt before the still basin in the study. Its water was meant to *reflect* not only a face but the state of one's inner words — the formulas a disciple held in the heart. My reflection shimmered and showed a glyph I had not yet learned. Shen Wujiu leaned close and said nothing for a long moment.
reflect:0.cnHint: 静水盆能____出弟子内心的法诀状态，我看见了一个陌生的符文。
reflect:0.hook: The glyph pulsed once, then vanished beneath still water.
reflect:0.line: 'The basin will *reflect* what you truly carry inside, not what you claim to know.'

attend:0.en: Xiaoxing shook my shoulder before dawn. 'You must *attend* the first-light lesson or Master Qingwu will seal your word-pouch for a week.' I rose, wrapped my robe tight, and followed her down the stone corridor. The lecture hall was already warm with candlelight and the low hum of disciples reciting root-words.
attend:0.cnHint: 小星提醒我必须____清晨的课，否则会被师尊封印词囊。
attend:0.hook: At the front of the hall, Master Qingwu's candle burned blue.
attend:0.line: 'You must *attend* the first-light lesson or lose your word-pouch for a week.'

belief:0.en: Master Qingwu placed a single seed-word on the table between us. 'A formula only works,' she said, 'when spoken with full *belief*. Doubt is a gap in the seal.' I had read that truth in every scroll, yet hearing it aloud made it feel heavier, like a stone dropped into deep water.
belief:0.cnHint: 师尊解释道，法诀只有在完全____的状态下才能生效，怀疑会让封印出现裂口。
belief:0.hook: The seed-word on the table began, very slowly, to glow.
belief:0.line: 'A formula only works when spoken with full *belief* — doubt is a gap in the seal.'

carry:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a small cloth bundle before I entered the archive room. 'You may *carry* three written formulas at most,' he said quietly. 'The room senses greed.' I tucked the bundle inside my robe, chose my three with care, and pushed open the heavy door. Cool air rushed out like a held breath released.
carry:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，进入典藏室最多只能____三份写好的法诀。
carry:0.hook: Behind me, the archive door shut with a sound like a word being swallowed.
carry:0.line: 'You may *carry* three written formulas at most — the room senses greed.'

else:0.en: I had studied the healing glyph for an hour, yet it would not light. Xiaoxing watched from the doorway. 'Try saying it softer,' she offered. I did. Nothing. 'What *else* can I do?' I asked, pressing my palms flat on the desk. She smiled, walked over, and tilted the scroll by a single degree toward the candle.
else:0.cnHint: 治愈符文始终无法激活，我问还有什么____方法可以尝试。
else:0.hook: The glyph lit — but in a colour no candle should make.
else:0.line: 'What *else* can you try when the method you know has already failed?'

prepare:0.en: Master Qingwu set a clay bowl before each of us at dawn. 'Before you may speak a single word of power,' she said, 'you must *prepare* the ground of your mind as a farmer prepares soil — clearing stones, smoothing earth.' I swept my thoughts clean and felt the room grow very still. Outside, a single white feather drifted upward against the wind.
prepare:0.cnHint: 清晨，师尊要求弟子们在开口念咒之前先____好内心的土壤。
prepare:0.hook: The feather rose higher, and no wind should have carried it there.
prepare:0.line: 'You must *prepare* your mind before the first word takes root.'

workplace:0.en: Shen Wujiu led me into the Hall of Brushes, where disciples grind ink and copy the living words onto silk. 'Think of this room as your *workplace*,' he said quietly, 'the way a smith thinks of his forge.' Every table held a candle, and every candle burned without smoke. Then one flame at the far end flickered and went dark on its own.
workplace:0.cnHint: 师兄带我进入笔墨堂，说这里是弟子们日常修炼的____。
workplace:0.hook: That candle had not been touched, yet it died as we watched.
workplace:0.line: 'This hall is your *workplace* — treat it with the same care as your own breath.'

post:0.en: Each morning a new instruction appeared on the notice board by the inner gate. Xiaoxing showed me how to read it. 'Master Qingwu will *post* the day's assigned word here at first light,' she whispered, her finger tracing the fresh ink. The board held only three characters today, but they shimmered as though the ink were still alive, and one character slowly changed shape before our eyes.
post:0.cnHint: 每天清晨，师尊会在告示板上____当日需要修习的字。
post:0.hook: The changing character formed a shape none of us had ever been taught.
post:0.line: 'Master Qingwu will *post* today's word before the morning bell rings.'

complete:0.en: I had been copying the healing word 'still' for an hour when Shen Wujiu glanced at my silk. 'You must *complete* every stroke,' he said, 'or the word will carry a crack no medicine can close.' I drew the final line and the character glowed faintly gold. From the mountain below our window, a low bell rang once — though no bell hung there.
complete:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，每一笔都必须____，否则字中会留下裂缝。
complete:0.hook: The bell rang once more, and the mountain had no bell tower.
complete:0.line: '*Complete* every stroke, or the word will never hold its power.'
